content.title: Stifling Defense Helps Orlando Magic Steal Game 1 in Detroit | Orlando Magic
content.text: Be the more physical team: CheckBe the more aggressive team: CheckLimit Detroit’s offensive rebounds: CheckLimit turnovers: CheckCapitalize in transition: CheckThe Orlando Magic checked those critical boxes and few others in a 112-101 Game 1 victory over the Detroit Pistons at Little Caesars Arena. As expected, this game was physical. Shots didn’t come easy. Detroit, as all teams do in the playoffs, especially at home, went on some runs. But the Magic stayed composed, they stayed aggressive, and they made several timely plays in the fourth quarter to go up 1-0 in this best-of-seven first round playoff series.“The competitive spirit that these guys showed to start the game, being able to battle through runs, and down the stretch being able to have a level of poise knowing things weren’t always going to go our way,” Magic head coach Jamahl Mosley said. “Our guys did a very good job of coming together and communicating the things that they saw — both offensively and defensively — that’s a big portion of it for me. When we communicate at this high level and understand exactly what everybody is trying to accomplish on both sides of the ball, I think this team can be pretty good.” The most significant stat was Orlando outscoring Detroit 54-34 in the paint. That’s remarkable because the Pistons ranked No. 1 during the regular season in that department with an average of 57.9 points in the paint.Also, the Pistons only came down with six offensive rebounds, seven fewer than their regular season average. The Magic only turned it over 12 times, they came up with 11 steals, and they scored 23 fast break points. The only thing that really kept Detroit hanging around was its free throw accumulation. It went 29-of-38 from the stripe. The Magic, even though they ranked No. 1 in the regular season in free throw attempts, went 14-of-19 from the line in Game 1. All five Magic starters scored in double figures. Paolo Banchero was hot early and finished with 23 points. Franz Wagner got going late and ended with 19 points. Desmond Bane, who was battling an illness, and Wendell Carter Jr. each scored 17 and Jalen Suggs had 16. Orlando, as a team, shot 49 percent from the field. Arguably, the two most important shots were made by Tristan da Silva and Carter on back-to-back possessions midway through the fourth. After the Pistons pulled within four with a pair of Cade Cunningham free throws, da Silva drilled a 3-pointer off a Carter sprayout and then Carter converted on a layup off a Bane assist to extend the lead back to nine.“Just being aggressive,” Banchero said. “I think it started with me and Jalen early on, and then Franz and Des shot going, Tristan hit a big shot, AB, Wendell was consistent the whole night. I think with the starters setting the tone, with the aggressiveness on offense, and guys just following along. I think guys feed off each other’s energy. I think us as a team having that communication throughout the game. It allows us to trust the hot hand or trust whatever we see out there, whoever has the advantage in terms of the offense. It was good to see everybody get an opportunity and get going at the right time. Ultimately, we got the win, so just want to try to keep that up."But really, the story was Orlando’s defense. It held Detroit to just 40 percent overall shooting from the floor and 31 percent from 3-point range. Cade Cunningham led the Pistons with 39 points. The only other Piston who scored in double figures was Tobias Harris, who finished with 17 points.Not including the Disney bubble in 2020, this was the Magic’s first road playoff victory since Game 1 of their 2019 first round series in Toronto. They had lost their last nine on the road in the postseason, 10 if you include the play-in tournament defeat in Philadelphia several days ago. Game 2 will be on Wednesday at 7 p.m. in Detroit. This contest will air on ESPN.
